answer: The inability to touch your opposite shoulder with your right arm and the stiffness in your shoulder likely indicate a postural imbalance, possibly involving a winged or rounded shoulder blade on the left side. This can result from tight pectoral and latissimus dorsi muscles pulling the shoulder forward, leading to restricted scapular mobility and reduced rib cage expansion.

key_points: A gentle breathing and scapular protraction exercise performed in a quadruped position to create space between the shoulder blades and the spine, promoting posterior ribcage expansion and improving scapular mobility. This helps to decompress tight tissues in the upper back.

This exercise builds on the side plank with overhead arm by adding an isometric push into the wall with the top hand to actively reposition the shoulder blade back onto the rib cage, improving scapular stability and congruence.

When the pectorals and latissimus dorsi are too short and overactive, they pull the shoulders forward, round the upper spine, and can push the lower spine into extension (hyper-lordosis). This creates a shortened and compressed spinal position and restricts rib cage expansion.
